store.tagline: Every Claude Code, Codex and Copilot session, and which one needs you
features: One row per session from the files the CLIs keep (`~/.claude/projects`, `~/.codex/sessions`, `~/.copilot/session-state`), by state: waiting on you, your turn, working, ended

The state from the transcript alone: a prompt or turn start after the last turn end is working; a tool call left without a result for 20 s while the process sits idle reads `waiting on you?`, the shape of a permission prompt; a hook can tell the exact state through `pal://sessions/state`
The pane: the last prompt, the assistant's last text, the pending tool call with its command or path, the agent and model, folder and branch, turns, tokens, permission mode, the transcript path

`enter` brings the session's terminal in front: a tmux pane, a kitty window (over its remote-control socket, found from kitty.conf), an iTerm2 or Terminal tab by tty, a WezTerm pane, else the app it runs under raised by its pid; on an ended session it opens a terminal with the resume command

`cmd+t` opens the transcript as a view inside pal: prompts, replies, tool calls with their outcome, thinking, streaming while the session runs; `[` for older entries, `c` copies the last reply, `s` types a line into a tmux-backed session
A line typed in the bar goes into a tmux-backed session with `cmd+enter`; `cmd+c` copies `claude --resume <id>`, `codex resume <id>` or `copilot --resume=<id>`; `cmd+d` kills
A bar item with the count and red, amber and blue segments per state, an alarm while a session waits on you, hidden with none; its popover a row per session with Enter, `o`, `r`, `x`, `s` and `p`
